messages:
Maya: Heads up 1: quick sync on run-history UX. Two contenders: "Split pane" (list + fixed details) vs "In-place expansion" (expand rows inline). Need accessibility and small-screen behavior.
Samir: Uploaded mock: https://figma.com/s/run-history-split-vs-inline. Main engineering concern: keyboard navigation and preserving list scroll position when opening details.
Eli: Keyboard plan: use roving tabindex on rows, Enter/Space toggles expansion, Escape closes and returns focus. For split pane, focus moves into panel but we must provide a skip-back link. Also aria-live when output streaming starts.
Nora: Microcopy: call the primary button on items "Invoke again" and the affordance for viewing schema "View params". Avoid jargon like "execution" in the UI copy.
Chris: Mobile constraints: split pane is awkward below 920px. Proposal: auto-switch to inline expansion + sticky header. Also we should debounce height changes so the page doesn't jump while streams append tokens.
Maya: Accessibility checklist: visible focus ring with 3px contrast border, role=button on row headers, aria-controls point to the detail region id, and ensure detail region has aria-hidden when collapsed.
Eli: UI detail: show a one-line collapsed preview of structured output (e.g. first key/value) with an arrow to expand full JSON. Use monospaced snippet and copy-to-clipboard icon.
Samir: Engineering note: backend will return a compact summary field in history list to avoid decompressing full payloads. Add an LRU cache on client for expanded items.
Nora: For function defs we should render params as pill chips: name + type, hover tooltip shows description. Long example payloads behind a "Show full example" link.
Maya: Copy nit: replace "history row" with "invocation item" in docs and dev comments. Keeps language consistent with API.
ci-bot: CI pipeline: playground/history-layout branch -> tests passed (12/12) at 2024-09-21T09:12:00Z.
Chris: Quick poll: reply with "Split" or "Inline". I prefer Inline for scanability.
Eli: Inline (less context switching)
Nora: Split (easier to compare outputs across runs)
Samir: Inline (simpler responsive behavior)
Maya: Thanks 1! Outcome: leaning Inline but we implement split-pane as an optional wide-screen mode behind a toggle. Eli, can you add keyboard flow to the prototype and include aria-live announcements for streaming? I'll update the ticket with accessibility checklist and copy changes.
Samir: I'll scope the client changes and add feature-flag gating for the split-pane toggle.
Maya: Perfect 44d. We'll review in next UX review on Thu.
